title: Winners announced for the 2026 Excellence in Road Safety Awards
source_name: 欧盟委员会交通与运输总司
content: Today, the Commission revealed the winners of its 2026 Excellence in Road Safety Awards, which celebrate outstanding and innovative efforts to improve road safety throughout Europe. The 2026 Winners are: - At Work: 5G Sandbox Innovation – RoadMaster VR (Lithuania) won for its immersive virtual reality training, which uses real-world driving footage and stress data to help international drivers safely revisit challenging situations and build confidence in unfamiliar road environments. - Education: Zavarovalnica Triglav (Slovenia) was recognised for DRAJV: Safer Driving App, which provides personalised feedback on speed, phone use, braking, acceleration and cornering to help drivers and motorcyclists improve their behaviour. - Technology: Roadscor (The Netherlands) won for Proactive Road Safety, which uses digital twins and infrastructure, traffic and behaviour data to help authorities identify risks and assess potential road safety improvements before changes are made. - Urban: Île-de-France Paris Region (France) received the award for VIF: A Safe Network for Vulnerable Road Users, an expanding network of safe cycling routes connecting municipalities and public transport hubs through consistent design standards and clear signage. - Vulnerable Road Users: Sialtrónica (Spain) won for Retrolight System®, which uses illuminated road markings, sensors and dynamic signage to improve visibility and safety at pedestrian crossings. - The People’s Choice Award went to Mettis AI (Spain) for improving drivers' training by combining artificial intelligence, computer vision, and vehicle data, voted for live by participants during the ceremony as the initiative that most inspired attendees. The Excellence in Road Safety Awards are part of the EU’s work to make Europe’s roads safer. In 2025 alone, 19,350 people lost their lives in a road crash. Background Every year, the awards recognise the most remarkable work by members of the European Road Safety Charter, including organisations, public authorities, and businesses, whose initiatives have made a meaningful difference to road safety across the continent. This year, 136 initiatives from 25 countries were submitted across five categories: At Work, Education, Technology, Urban and Vulnerable Road Users. Road safety is a shared responsibility between the EU and Member States. While national and local authorities deliver most day-to-day actions, the EU contributes with safety rules for infrastructure and vehicles and for driving testing and licencing, coordinates cross-border cooperation between authorities and efforts to exchange best practices, and funds road safety projects. The EU set itself a 50% reduction target for road deaths and serious injuries by 2030, while aiming to reach close to zero road deaths by 2050 (‘Vision Zero’). In 2026, the Commission published a report on the Implementation of the EU Road Safety Policy Framework at the Mid-Point. The report confirms that significant progress has been made in reducing road fatalities, but the current pace is still insufficient.
